headline: Citigroup loses $9.8 billion and cuts its dividend
text: Citigroup, led since December by new chief executive Vikram Pandit, reported a fourth-quarter net loss of $9.83 billion after $18.1 billion of write-downs and credit costs on subprime exposures, cut its dividend, and raised $12.5 billion in a private sale of convertible preferred shares to long-term investors, plus about $2 billion more in the market. With the Abu Dhabi deal it has raised almost $30 billion in two months.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465908002661/a08-1961_1ex99d1.htm (Citigroup press release, 15 January 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465908002663/a08-1948_1ex99d1.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000114420408003260/v100398_ex99-1.htm (22 January 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000114420407066977/v096976_ex99-1.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: 388 Greenwich Street, Citigroup's building in Lower Manhattan

headline: Record results, weak forecast, falling market
text: On 22 January Apple reported its best quarter ever: revenue of 9.6 billion dollars, up 35%, and a profit of 1.58 billion, with 2.3 million iPhones sold. But it forecast revenue of only about 6.8 billion dollars for the next quarter, and stock markets are falling.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs with the MacBook Air, Macworld, San Francisco, 15 January 2008

headline: Meg Whitman steps down at eBay
text: Meg Whitman, who has run eBay since 1998 when it had 30 employees, resigned as chief executive and was replaced by John Donahoe. Whitman remains on the board.
imageCaption: Meg Whitman, eBay's chief executive

headline: The Fed's emergency cut: three-quarters of a point between meetings
text: As shares fell around the world, the Federal Reserve cut its key rate by 0.75 percentage point to 3.5 percent on 22 January without waiting for its meeting, its largest cut in 25 years, and by another half point on 30 January. The S&P 500 still lost 6% in January to 1,378.55.
imageCaption: Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke pauses during a hearing of the House Budget Committee, Washington, 17 January 2008

headline: Mismarked positions in the CDO business
text: Credit Suisse has found mismarks and pricing errors by a small number of traders on certain asset-backed positions in its CDO trading business. Markets for mortgage-linked securities remain in turmoil.
imageCaption: Walter Kielholz, chairman of Credit Suisse, at the St. Gallen Symposium

headline: Microsoft bids 44.6 billion dollars for Yahoo
text: On 1 February Microsoft offered to buy Yahoo for 31 dollars a share, half in cash and half in shares, about 44.6 billion dollars and a 62% premium. Microsoft wants to compete with Google in online advertising, which it expects to double from 40 billion dollars in 2007 to nearly 80 billion by 2010.
imageCaption: Yahoo's headquarters in Sunnyvale, California
imageCredit: user Coolcaesar. User Coolcaesar on en.wikipedia

headline: Bear Stearns falls, and fears turn to Lehman
text: Bear Stearns, the smallest of the big Wall Street firms, ran out of cash and was sold to JPMorgan Chase for $2 a share with Federal Reserve support on 16 March; analysts named Lehman as the next firm at risk. Lehman answered on 18 March with a first-quarter profit of $489 million and a cash reserve of $34 billion at the parent company, and its shares jumped 46% that day. They still ended the month down by a quarter.
imageCaption: Lehman Brothers headquarters, New York, 31 March 2008

headline: Bear Stearns is rescued by JPMorgan for 2 dollars a share
text: The investment bank Bear Stearns, heavy with 46 billion dollars of mortgage assets, faced collapse in mid-March. On 16-17 March JPMorgan Chase agreed to buy it for 2 dollars a share, with the Fed guaranteeing bad loans; the shares were at 60 dollars a week earlier and 178 a year ago. The Fed cut its key rate by another 0.75 point to 2.25 percent on 18 March.
imageCaption: A woman walks out of the Bear Stearns headquarters on Madison Avenue, New York, 24 March 2008

headline: Altria spins off Philip Morris International
text: On 28 March Altria completed the spin-off of Philip Morris International, giving one PMI share for each Altria share. PMI, which sells Marlboro and other brands outside the United States, trades separately from 31 March. Altria keeps Philip Morris USA and is moving its headquarters to Richmond, Virginia.
imageCaption: A pack of Marlboro, the brand Philip Morris International takes with it into the world, August 2007

headline: Vale talks collapse over Glencore's marketing rights
text: Talks for Vale to buy Xstrata ended in late March without agreement. Vale's chief Roger Agnelli said they broke down over Glencore's demand to keep, and extend, its rights to market the merged group's metals; Mick Davis said only that the two sides could not reach an agreement. Xstrata shares fell more than 12% at the opening on the news.
imageCaption: A monument at Vale's railway and port at Vitoria, Brazil

headline: Ospel goes after another $19 billion write-down
text: On 1 April UBS pre-announced a first-quarter net loss of about 12 billion francs on $19 billion of write-downs on US real-estate assets, a fully underwritten rights issue of about 15 billion francs and a separate unit for its bad mortgage positions. Chairman Marcel Ospel is not standing for re-election; the general counsel, Peter Kurer, was elected chairman at the meeting on 23 April. Investors were relieved: the shares rose 15% in dollars in April.
source: UBS Form 20-F/A for 2007, filed 14 April 2008, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1114446/000095012308004121/y54449e20vfza.htm (read 2026-10-03); UBS Form 20-F for 2008, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1114446/000095012309004436/y75024e20vf.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Marcel Ospel (right) at his last general meeting as chairman of UBS, with his successor Peter Kurer, 23 April 2008

headline: GE misses its numbers for the first time in years
text: On 11 April General Electric reported first-quarter earnings per share of 44 cents, down 8%, and cut its full-year forecast to 2.20 to 2.30 dollars. Chairman Jeff Immelt said the financial services businesses were hit by a slowing US economy and difficult capital markets, and that he was disappointed.
imageCaption: General Electric chief executive Jeffrey Immelt (left) in Warsaw

headline: Lehman raises $4 billion
text: Lehman Brothers raised $4 billion of new capital by selling convertible preferred shares. Its shares recovered part of their March losses.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908038647/a08-16256_1ex99d1.htm (Lehman press release, 9 June 2008, reporting the April issue; read 2026-10-03)

headline: Hedge fund manager attacks Lehman's accounting
text: David Einhorn of Greenlight Capital, who said in April that he is betting against Lehman's shares, publicly questioned the firm's accounting for its real-estate holdings after a call with finance chief Erin Callan. Lehman's shares fell 17% in May.
imageCaption: The Lehman Brothers building, Times Square, New York

headline: Rights issue: seven new shares for every twenty
text: UBS shareholders received one free share for every 20 held (record date 25 April, delivered 19 May) instead of a dividend, and then subscription rights for the 15-billion-franc capital increase: for every 20 rights, holders can buy seven new shares at 21 francs. The shares trade ex-rights from the end of May. On 20 May UBS also sold $15 billion of US mortgage securities to a fund run by BlackRock, lending most of the money itself.

headline: Lehman's first loss: $2.8 billion; president and finance chief out
text: Lehman Brothers announced on 9 June its first quarterly loss as a public company, about $2.8 billion, as mortgage and real-estate holdings fell in value and some hedges failed, and said it was raising $6 billion of new capital. It said it had cut its leverage from 31.7 times its equity to under 25. On 12 June president Joseph Gregory and finance chief Erin Callan were replaced. The shares fell 46% in the month.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908038647/a08-16256_1ex99d1.htm (Lehman press release, 9 June 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908040477/a08-15739_16ex99d1.htm (12 June 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Lehman Brothers headquarters, New York, 31 March 2008

headline: Record oil and bank losses send shares down 9 percent
text: Oil jumped nearly 11 dollars on 6 June to a record 138.54 dollars a barrel, raising fears of inflation and recession at once. Banks kept reporting mortgage losses: Wachovia, the fourth-largest American bank, ousted its chief executive on 2 June, and General Motors announced plant closures and 10,000 job cuts. The S&P 500 lost 9% in June to 1,280.00.
imageCaption: A trader bites his nails on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as shares slide to a three-month low, 20 June 2008
imageCredit: Photo by Jin Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images

headline: The App Store opens
text: Apple opened the App Store on 10 July with 500 programs, 125 of them free, that anyone can download to an iPhone. There were 10 million downloads in the first weekend. Outside developers write the programs, and Apple takes a share of the sales.
imageCaption: The original iPhone (left) next to the new iPhone 3G, July 2008

headline: Oil hits 145 dollars, then falls back
text: US crude closed at a record of about 145 dollars a barrel in early July, then fell back to about 124 by month's end. On 31 July ExxonMobil reported second-quarter profit of 11.68 billion dollars, up 14 percent on a year earlier, but the shares fell as investors worried the oil spike would not last.
source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 31 July 2008, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408808000102/r8k2q991.htm (read 2026-10-03); data/out/xom.json and data/reference/sp500.json (2008 changes, for the why)
imageCaption: A petrol station sign that has run out of fours: regular at $4.03, July 2008

headline: Novartis buys a quarter of Alcon from Nestlé
text: Novartis has bought about 25% of the eye-care company Alcon of Fort Worth, Texas, from Nestlé, which still owns the majority.
imageCaption: Fence artwork at the Novartis campus, Basel

headline: Faulty notebook chips and a profit warning
text: On 2 July Nvidia said it will take a charge of 150 to 200 million dollars to cover repairs and replacements of some older notebook graphics and chipset products that fail because of a weak packaging material. All products now shipping use a more robust material.
imageCaption: Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California

headline: Russia goes to war with Georgia
text: After Georgian forces moved into the breakaway region of South Ossetia on 7 August, Russia sent in troops and aircraft, drove them out and advanced into Georgia proper. A ceasefire brokered by French President Nicolas Sarkozy was agreed on 12 August. On 26 August Russia recognised South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states.
imageCaption: Georgian troops near Gori, 9 August 2008

headline: Beijing Olympics: Federer and Wawrinka win doubles gold
text: At the Olympics in Beijing, Roger Federer and Stanislas Wawrinka won gold in the men's tennis doubles, and Fabian Cancellara won the cycling time trial.

headline: Xstrata bids £5bn for Lonmin as commodities turn
text: On 6 August Xstrata said it would offer £33 a share in cash, about £5bn ($10bn), for the platinum producer Lonmin, a 42% premium; Lonmin rejected it as opportunistic and its shares jumped above the offer price. Commodity prices fell in August: copper averaged $7,635 a tonne against $8,414 in July, coal $158 against $180, and oil dropped from its July record.
source: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/26135/lonmin-snubs-takeover-offer-by-xstrata; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Lonmin's platinum mines at Marikana, South Africa

headline: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
text: After talks with Bank of America and Barclays failed over the weekend and the government refused to back a rescue, Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 15 September, with $639 billion of assets and debts of $613 billion to banks, the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history. The shares fell more than 90% that day and were removed from the New York Stock Exchange; the Dow Jones fell more than 500 points. Barclays agreed to buy Lehman's North American business for a fraction of its former value.
imageCaption: Photographers surround a man carrying a box out of Lehman Brothers' headquarters on the morning of the bankruptcy filing, New York, 15 September 2008

headline: In the panic, Buffett invests in Goldman Sachs
text: On 23 September, in the middle of the financial panic, Berkshire bought perpetual preferred stock in Goldman Sachs paying a 10% dividend. Buffett's money is read as a vote of confidence in the battered investment bank.
imageCaption: The Goldman Sachs headquarters, West Street, New York

headline: The House votes down the bailout and the Dow falls 778 points
text: On 20 September Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson asked Congress for 700 billion dollars to buy toxic mortgage assets ('If it doesn't pass, then heaven help us all'). On 29 September the House of Representatives rejected the bill 225 to 208; the Dow fell 777.68 points, its largest point drop ever, and the S&P 500 8.8%. The S&P 500 ended September down 9% at 1,166.36.
imageCaption: Traders on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as the House rejects the 700 billion dollar rescue plan, 29 September 2008

headline: Credit crisis hits the miners
text: The failure of Lehman Brothers and the freezing of credit markets in September have hit mining shares hardest. Copper averaged $6,991 a tonne, down 17% from July, and iron ore and coal prices are falling as Chinese steel mills cut output. Investors are questioning the debt taken on by acquisitive miners; Xstrata has been spending heavily on a stake in Lonmin since August.
source: Xstrata circular 2 Feb 2009 (current trading and prospects), https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/6630M_-2009-2-2.pdf; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Reporters outside Lehman Brothers' headquarters, New York, 15 September 2008

headline: The first Android phone
text: On 23 September T-Mobile announced the G1, made by HTC, the first phone using Android, Google's free operating system for phones. It will cost 179 dollars with a two-year contract from 20 October.
imageCaption: The T-Mobile G1, the first Android phone, at its launch event in New York, 23 September 2008

headline: The Swiss state rescues UBS
text: On 16 October the Swiss National Bank and the federal government announced measures to strengthen the Swiss financial system. UBS can transfer up to $60 billion of illiquid securities, mostly backed by US home and commercial mortgages, to a fund controlled by the National Bank, which lends it up to $54 billion; UBS puts in up to $6 billion of equity. The Confederation subscribes 6 billion francs of mandatory convertible notes in UBS. Credit Suisse, which raised capital privately, does not use the facility.
source: Swiss National Bank, media release of 16 October 2008, https://www.snb.ch/public/asset/de/www-snb-ch/publications/communication/press-releases/2008/pre_20081016_1/publications0/pre_20081016_1.de.pdf (read 2026-10-03); UBS Form 20-F for 2008 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jean-Pierre Roth of the National Bank (second from left) and federal councillor Eveline Widmer-Schlumpf (fourth from left) present the rescue package for UBS, Bern, 16 October 2008

headline: Credit Suisse raises 10 billion francs without the state
text: On 16 October, the day the Swiss state rescued UBS, Credit Suisse announced it had raised new capital from a small group of investors, about 10 billion francs from three existing shareholders; Qatar Holding reported holding 8.9% of the shares on 22 October. Credit Suisse said it would not use the National Bank's facility for illiquid assets. The bank cancelled its share buyback.
source: Credit Suisse Form 20-F for 2008, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053092/000137036809000006/a090324ar20f.htm (read 2026-10-03); Swiss National Bank, media release of 16 October 2008 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Brady Dougan, chief executive of Credit Suisse, at the St. Gallen Symposium

headline: Buffett backs GE as it raises 15 billion dollars
text: On 1 October General Electric announced it will sell at least 12 billion dollars of new shares to the public and 3 billion dollars of preferred stock with a 10% dividend to Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, which also gets warrants to buy GE shares at 22.25 dollars. 'GE is the symbol of American business to the world,' Buffett said. Jeff Immelt said GE remains committed to its triple-A rating and is meeting its commercial paper needs.
imageCaption: Warren Buffett, whose Berkshire Hathaway agreed to invest in General Electric

headline: Crash month: the worst week ever, then the biggest daily gain since the 1930s
text: Congress passed the 700 billion dollar rescue on 3 October, but panic spread worldwide: in the week of 6 to 10 October the Dow fell 18.2%, its worst week ever, and on 8 October central banks cut rates together in an emergency move. On 13 October the S&P 500 jumped 11.6%, then fell 9.0% on 15 October and rose 10.8% on 28 October. The S&P 500 lost 17% in October to 968.75, its worst month since the 1987 crash.
imageCaption: A trader rubs his face on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as the Dow closes more than 500 points down, 7 October 2008

headline: Government rescues Citigroup
text: On 17 November Citigroup announced about 52,000 more job cuts, and its market value fell to about $20 billion from $244 billion two years earlier. On 23 November the Treasury, the Federal Reserve and the FDIC agreed to guarantee losses on $306 billion of Citigroup's loans and securities and to invest a further $20 billion. In return the government gets preferred shares and warrants, a say in pay and lending, and the dividend is cut to a cent a share.
imageCaption: Henry Paulson, US Treasury Secretary

headline: China announces a 4 trillion yuan stimulus
text: On 9 November China's State Council announced a stimulus of 4 trillion yuan, about $586 billion, with 1.5 trillion for railways, roads and other infrastructure and money for earthquake rebuilding and cheap housing. Growth has fallen towards 6% from double digits.
imageCaption: Investors watch share prices in Chongqing the day after China announced its 4 trillion yuan stimulus, 10 November 2008

headline: Obama is elected president
text: Barack Obama won the US presidency on 4 November with 365 electoral votes to 173 for John McCain and 52.9 percent of the vote, the first African American elected president. He takes office in January in the middle of the worst financial crisis since the 1930s and two wars.
imageCaption: The crowd in Grant Park, Chicago, listens to John McCain's concession on election night, 4 November 2008

headline: Zero interest rates and the Fed starts buying bonds
text: On 16 December the Fed cut its rate target to a range of 0 to 0.25 percent, the lowest ever, and said rates would stay exceptionally low 'for some time'. On 25 November it had announced it would buy up to 500 billion dollars of mortgage bonds and 100 billion of mortgage-agency debt, and it is considering buying Treasury bonds as well. The 10-year Treasury yield averaged 2.4 percent in December, and consumer prices in November were only 1.1 percent higher than a year earlier. Long Treasury bonds gained about a quarter in November and December.
imageCaption: Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke speaks at a conference on housing and mortgage markets, Washington, 4 December 2008

headline: 2008 in review: shares lose 38 percent
text: The S&P 500 fell 38% in 2008 to 903.25, its worst year in the game's data, and the Dow 33.8% to 8,776.39. On 1 December economists declared that a recession had begun in December 2007, and the S&P 500 fell 8.9% that day. On 16 December the Federal Reserve cut its key rate to between 0 and 0.25 percent, as low as it can go.
imageCaption: Traders in the Merrill Lynch booth on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange after the closing bell on the last trading day of 2008, 31 December 2008

headline: Copper at a four-year low, mines shut
text: Copper averaged $3,072 a tonne in December, down 63% from July, and thermal coal $79, less than half its summer peak. Xstrata is suspending or closing higher-cost production and cutting spending. Markets worry how it will carry its debt, which stood at well over $15bn after the Falconbridge and Lonmin purchases.
source: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages; Xstrata circular 2 Feb 2009, https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/6630M_-2009-2-2.pdf (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: An open-pit copper mine at Elshitsa, Bulgaria

headline: Siemens settles the bribery case for about $1.4 billion
text: On 15 December Siemens agreed to pay about 1.4 billion dollars to US and German authorities to settle the bribery charges, including a 350 million dollar payment to the SEC and 569 million to the Munich prosecutor. The SEC called it the largest settlement in the history of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. The euro also recovered strongly in December.
imageCaption: Siemens headquarters on Wittelsbacherplatz, Munich
